thinh_vu: Thính Vũ Lâu, the Tower Where One Listens to the Rain, a stormy southern ma đạo house: a long black oiled-silk rain cloak with a high collar over a robe of fine undyed grey cloth, well cut and clean; a wide round straw rain hat, plain, worn or hanging at the back on a cord; the Thunder Hall's cloaks are scorched at the hems with dark burn-marks and are never mended; inner disciples add a narrow black silk sash, elders a cloak of heavier glossy silk with a darker lining; the sleeves are close and practical; no bright colour anywhere, everything the colour of wet slate, ink and straw.
minh_loan: Minh Loan Các, the Pavilion of the Singing Bells, bronze casters of a western coast and mountain: robes of fine bronze-brown wool, closely woven and well fitted, with a plain round collar; casters add a clay-grey leather apron over the front, the outer gate has clay dried on the forearms to the elbow; inner disciples have a thin bronze-coloured thread along the hem and cuffs, elders and the head a collar band of bronze thread; a small bronze bell on a cord at the belt or in the hand; sleeves pushed back for work; clean cloth, only the clay and soot of the trade on it.
vong_trieu: Vọng Triều Đường, the Hall Watching the Tide, lamp-keepers of the western shore towers: a knee-length coat of oiled grey cloth, closed with toggles, well cut and kept clean, over plain dark trousers and a grey inner shirt; a brass lamp-hook hanging from the belt; the elders carry a lit storm lamp, a small square lantern of brass and horn glass with a warm yellow flame; sea-weather colours, grey, brass and lamp-yellow; hair tied back tight against the wind.
chan_kim: Chân Kim Các, the Pavilion of True Gold, assayers who weigh ore and metal in public: assayers wear a short blue miners' jacket of heavy cotton, clean and square-shouldered, over fine merchants' silk in a muted colour (wine, mustard or dark green); a leather pouch or a small set of brass weights and a tiny brass balance are the tools; sleeves rolled to the elbow; the more senior the assayer, the finer the silk beneath the same blue jacket; no jewellery except a fine metal pin or ring, the house takes no element as its own so no colour belongs to the house but the blue of the jacket.
ngao_tuyet: Ngạo Tuyết Phái, the School That Defies the Snow, mountain swordsmen: white hemp robes in every season, finely woven, clean and wrinkle-free, cut as a plain crossed-collar robe with a wide cloth belt; a small plum-branch pin of dark wood at the hair or collar, with two or three tiny pale pink blossoms; bare feet even in the snow; the sword is plain, in a plain scabbard; hair simple; the only colour is the plum pin.
